questions.question: Which organizational data can Microsoft 365 Copilot surface to a user?
options: Only data the user already has at least view access to, using the same access controls as other Microsoft 365 services
Any file in the tenant, regardless of who can open it
Only files the user personally created or owns
Anything, because it temporarily elevates the user's access
questions.explanation: Copilot respects existing permissions: it only surfaces content a user can already access, using the same underlying access controls as the rest of Microsoft 365.

questions.question: Your prompts, responses, and data accessed through Microsoft Graph are not used to train the foundation large language models.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Under enterprise data protection, prompts, responses, and Microsoft Graph data are not used to train the foundation models used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

questions.question: Because Copilot's responses are not guaranteed to be fully factual, what should users do?
options: Review and fact-check the output before relying on it or sharing it
Trust it fully, since Microsoft certifies every answer
Nothing, because Copilot sends drafts automatically
Assume it is always accurate
questions.explanation: Copilot can occasionally be wrong, so responsible use means reviewing and fact-checking its output before you rely on it or send it to others.

questions.question: Select all that are true about how Microsoft 365 Copilot protects data.
options: It honors Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels and the user's usage rights
Customer content is logically isolated between tenants
Data is encrypted both at rest and in transit
It pools data from all tenants into one shared index
questions.explanation: Copilot inherits sensitivity labels and usage rights, keeps tenants logically isolated, and encrypts data at rest and in transit. It does not pool tenant data into a shared index.

questions.question: Select all of Microsoft's recommended practices for rolling out Copilot.
options: Begin with a limited pilot to a small group of users
Gather feedback and build internal champions who support broader adoption
Measure adoption and business impact with built-in reporting such as the Copilot Dashboard and admin usage reports
Enable Copilot for everyone at once and skip any pilot
Measure success solely by the number of licenses purchased
questions.explanation: Microsoft recommends a phased rollout: pilot with a small group, build champions, and measure impact with tools like the Copilot Dashboard. A big-bang launch and license counts are not the recommended approach.

questions.question: Why is remediating oversharing an important step before deploying Copilot?
options: Because Copilot can surface any content a user already has access to, so a governed data foundation reduces risk
Because Copilot only ever accesses public files
Because Copilot cannot read SharePoint content
Because getting data ready mainly means deleting all old files
questions.explanation: Since Copilot surfaces content users can already reach, remediating oversharing and excessive permissions first creates a secure, governed data foundation and lowers risk.
